title: What Is System Design?
summary: What system design is, functional vs non-functional requirements, and the reliability/scalability/maintainability lens — plus why every design is a set of trade-offs.

title: Scalability, Availability & Performance
summary: Latency vs throughput, why we measure with percentiles (p99), what availability 'nines' mean in real downtime, and SLI/SLO/SLA.

title: Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation
summary: Size a system fast: powers of two, the latency numbers every engineer should know, and estimating QPS, storage, and bandwidth from stated assumptions.

title: How the Internet Works for Designers
summary: IP, TCP vs UDP, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS and TLS, why round trips dominate latency, and how CDNs bring content closer to users.

title: Designing APIs: REST, RPC & GraphQL
summary: REST, gRPC, and GraphQL compared; HTTP methods and which are safe/idempotent; pagination, versioning, and idempotency keys for safe retries.

title: Storage Foundations: SQL vs NoSQL
summary: The relational model and ACID, the four NoSQL families, ACID vs BASE, and how to choose storage by data model and access patterns — without the scaling myths.

title: Caching
summary: Cache-aside, read-through, write-through, and write-back; eviction and TTLs; why invalidation is hard; and preventing cache stampedes.

title: Load Balancing & Reverse Proxies
summary: How load balancers give scale and availability, Layer 4 vs Layer 7, balancing algorithms, health checks, and reverse proxies.

title: Scaling Out: Statelessness & the Scaling Cube
summary: Why stateless services are the key to horizontal scaling, where state should live, and the AKF Scale Cube’s three axes.

title: Database Replication
summary: Leader–follower replication, synchronous vs asynchronous, replication lag and read anomalies, and the hazards of failover.

title: Partitioning (Sharding)
summary: Range vs hash partitioning, consistent hashing and what it actually solves, hotspots, routing, and rebalancing.

title: Consistency Models
summary: Strong (linearizable) vs eventual consistency, the useful middle grounds, and the crucial difference between linearizability and serializability.

title: The CAP Theorem & PACELC
summary: The CAP theorem stated precisely (CP vs AP during a partition), why 'pick 2 of 3' misleads, and how PACELC adds the everyday latency-vs-consistency trade-off.

title: Messaging & Event Streaming
summary: Queues vs logs, delivery semantics, why exactly-once delivery is generally impossible (and what systems really provide), and backpressure.

title: Reliable Communication: Idempotency, Retries & Timeouts
summary: Why a timeout leaves the outcome unknown, choosing timeouts, retries with exponential backoff and jitter, and idempotency keys for safe writes.

title: Rate Limiting & API Gateways
summary: Token bucket, leaky bucket, and window algorithms; responding with 429; and what an API gateway does at the edge.

title: Monoliths vs Microservices
summary: The real trade-offs, how to draw service boundaries, the distributed-monolith anti-pattern, and why starting with a monolith is common advice.

title: Resilience Patterns
summary: Containing partial failure with timeouts, circuit breakers, bulkheads, graceful degradation, load shedding, and service discovery.

title: Distributed Transactions: Saga, 2PC & Outbox
summary: Why cross-service atomicity is hard, two-phase commit’s blocking cost, the saga pattern, and the transactional outbox for reliable events.

title: Consensus & Coordination
summary: What consensus is and why it's hard, quorums and the majority rule, how Raft elects a leader and replicates a log, and coordination services.

title: Designing for Failure
summary: Eliminating single points of failure with redundancy across failure domains, replication vs backups, and disaster recovery with RTO and RPO.

title: Observability: Logs, Metrics & Traces
summary: The three pillars — logs, metrics, and traces — the RED and USE methods, alerting on symptoms not causes, and OpenTelemetry.

title: Security Essentials
summary: Authentication vs authorization, encryption in transit and at rest, OAuth 2.0 and OIDC, least privilege, and avoiding classic security mistakes.

title: Capstone: Designing a System End to End
summary: A repeatable framework — requirements, estimation, API, data, scaling, resilience, trade-offs — applied end to end to a URL shortener.
